subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Topology Optimization: Removing What Isn't Needed
description: A quick, practical guide to Topology Optimization: Removing What Isn't Needed.

hook.text: Start with a solid block of material. Tell the computer where the forces go. It removes every gram that isn't carrying load.

buildup.text: Topology optimization distributes material only where stress flows. The result is a skeleton — minimum weight, maximum strength.

discovery.text: The algorithm divides the block into millions of tiny elements. Each is evaluated: does it carry load? If not, it's removed.

twist.text: Optimized parts often can't be made traditionally. Internal voids and organic curves require 3D printing to produce.

climax.text: GE's LEAP fuel nozzle was topology-optimized from 20 parts into one. It's 25% lighter and five times more durable.

punchline.text: Start full. Remove everything unnecessary. What remains is engineering.

quiz.question: What did topology optimization achieve for GE's LEAP fuel nozzle?
options: It doubled fuel efficiency by changing the nozzle's spray pattern geometry
It reduced 20 separate parts into one that was 25% lighter and five times more durable
It eliminated the need for heat-resistant coatings by changing the material
